findings.headline: The title labels the survey instead of inviting participation
findings.evidence: Member's Mark Boxer Briefs Feedback Survey
findings.explanation: Keep the specific product name, but use sentence case and an invitation to share a perspective.
findings.member_impact: A welcoming title makes the survey feel like a conversation rather than an administrative task.

findings.headline: The welcome leaves out the purpose and the member's role
findings.evidence: Welcome to the Boxer Briefs Survey! This takes about 3 minutes.
findings.explanation: Explain what you want to learn and why this member was invited. Invite the member to contribute as a co-creator rather than simply complete a survey. This also covers criterion 1.3. Fill in the bracketed facts before publishing. The rewrite preserves the existing timing statement because its accuracy is already flagged separately.
findings.member_impact: Members cannot tell why their perspective matters or what they are being invited to help explore.

findings.headline: The closing gives a status message instead of thanks
findings.explanation: Thank members for their time and perspective, then briefly explain how their answers will be used. This also covers criterion 10.3 and the cold closing under criterion 9.1. Replace the bracketed text with a confirmed use of the answers, without promising changes or follow-up you cannot guarantee.
findings.member_impact: Members finish without feeling appreciated or knowing what will happen with their answers.
